name: Question 8
problem:
Evaluate the mixed integral

$$
{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{x}2xyz\,\text{d}y]\text{d}A
$$

given that the region $D$ in the $xz$-plane is given by

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le \sqrt{4-2z},\,0\le z\le 2}.
$$
worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{x}2xyz\,\text{d}y]\text{d}A & ={∬}_{D}xz[{y}^{2}]_{y=0}^{y=x}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}{x}^{3}z\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $D$ is a type II region in the $xz$-plane.
Therefore, to evaluate our double integral as a repeated integral over this region, we integrate with respect to $x$ and then with respect to $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}{x}^{3}z\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-2z}}{x}^{3}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}z[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-2z}}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}z{[\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}]}_{x=0}^{x=\sqrt{4-2z}}\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{4}(4-2z)^{2}z\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}4z-4{z}^{2}+{z}^{3}\,\text{d}z \\  & ={[2{z}^{2}-\frac{4}{3}{z}^{3}+\frac{1}{4}{z}^{4}]}_{z=0}^{z=2} \\  & =(8-\frac{32}{3}+4)-0 \\  & =\frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
